questions.question: Within what time limit must a controller notify a personal data breach to the supervisory authority?
questions.expected_answer: Without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of it (Art. 33(1)).

expected_evidence.snippet: not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it

questions.question: What is the minimum age at which a child can give valid consent for information society services under the GDPR, and may Member States lower it?
questions.expected_answer: 16 years; Member States may provide a lower age, but not below 13 years (Art. 8(1)).

questions.question: In which cases must a controller or processor designate a data protection officer?
questions.expected_answer: Public authority/body (except courts); core activities requiring regular and systematic large-scale monitoring; large-scale processing of special categories or criminal data (Art. 37(1)).

expected_evidence.snippet: the processing is carried out by a public authority or body

questions.question: How long does a controller have to respond to a data subject's request under Articles 15 to 22, and can this period be extended?
questions.expected_answer: Without undue delay and within one month of receipt; extendable by two further months where necessary (Art. 12(3)).

questions.question: What must a provider of a publicly available electronic communications service do to safeguard the security of its services under the ePrivacy Directive?
questions.expected_answer: Take appropriate technical and organisational measures, if necessary together with the network provider (Art. 4(1) Directive 2002/58/EC).

questions.question: What is the maximum notice period for initiating the switching process that a contract with a provider of data processing services may require under the Data Act?
questions.expected_answer: A maximum notice period for initiation of switching which shall not exceed two months (Art. 25(2)(d)).

questions.question: Under the GDPR, what is the maximum fine a company can receive, and which kinds of violations trigger the higher fine?
questions.expected_answer: Up to EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover (whichever is higher) for infringements of basic processing principles/consent, data subject rights, third-country transfers etc. (Art. 83(5)); the lower tier is EUR 10 million / 2% (Art. 83(4)).

questions.question: When processing relies on consent, what must the controller be able to demonstrate, and how easy must it be for the data subject to withdraw consent?
questions.expected_answer: The controller must be able to demonstrate that the data subject consented (Art. 7(1)); withdrawing must be as easy as giving consent (Art. 7(3)).

expected_evidence.snippet: able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented
right to withdraw his or her consent at any time

questions.question: Which article of the ePrivacy Directive governs storing information on a user's terminal equipment, and which GDPR article sets the conditions for consent?
questions.expected_answer: ePrivacy Directive Article 5(3) (storage/access to terminal equipment only with clear information and the right to refuse); GDPR Article 7 (conditions for consent).

expected_evidence.snippet: terminal equipment of a subscriber or user

questions.question: What must a controller do about a personal data breach towards the supervisory authority and towards the affected individuals, and when is communication to individuals not required?
questions.expected_answer: Notify the authority within 72 hours (Art. 33); communicate to data subjects without undue delay when there is a high risk (Art. 34(1)); not required if e.g. data were encrypted, high risk is no longer likely, or it would involve disproportionate effort (Art. 34(3)).

expected_evidence.snippet: communicate the personal data breach to the data subject
shall not be required if any of the following conditions are met

questions.question: What happens if the Data Act conflicts with Union data protection law, and when is the processing of personal data lawful under the GDPR?
questions.expected_answer: In a conflict, the Union or national data protection law prevails (Data Act Art. 1(5)); processing is lawful only if at least one of the Art. 6(1) GDPR legal bases applies.
